findings.title: The status strip does not follow the GMs' stores it reads: an Eclipse crossing, a Monocub's purse and a death the GMs keep leave it showing the old count
findings.where: scripts/player-status.mjs:40-75 (its listeners) against 432-562 and 608-660 (what it reads); settings.mjs:3233-3247, 3483-3494; sync.mjs:485
findings.what_happens: In an Eclipse the strip draws a player's Move feet from eclipse.mjs movesLeft and the GM's Still placing from stillPlacing, both read off the GMs' store eclipseMoves on a GM and the owner's copy mineEclipseMoves on a player (settings.mjs:3933-3943). A crossing patches the store on the primary (eclipse.mjs:1229) and sends the owner's copy (1247); both are client settings whose onChange runs the sync kind `visibility`, whose row is visibility, sheets and hud (sync.mjs:485). The strip is redrawn by none of them: it hears updateActor, its six settings through updateSetting, updateUser, drpgEclipseChanged and canvasReady, and a crossing in an Eclipse writes no actor (movement.mjs:2781-2802 returns before any charge). The same holds for a Monocub's Hope, which the strip counts with its purse (player-status.mjs:543-547; the purse is the store gmCubs or the copy mineCubs, monocub.mjs:246-250), whose change calls drpgCubsChanged and refreshes the sheets only (settings.mjs:3483-3486), and for the GM's Still to act, which counts with isDeadForGm (monokuma.mjs:120-123), whose store change runs `visibility` and drpgDeathsChanged (settings.mjs:3491-3494). The sheet and the clock are redrawn; the strip beside them is not, until some student's actor is written or the scene changes.
findings.failure_scenario: In a Morning Eclipse a player drags their token through one door: the sheet's Move tile says one crossing left, the strip under the clock still shows both feet lit, and the GM's strip still reads Still placing 5 / 5 until somebody's sheet is written.
findings.expected: the strip redrawn on each source it reads - the crossings' store and copy, the Monocubs' record, the deaths kept - as the sheets and the clock are
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for any other caller of renderPlayerStatus outside the tests (grep: none but its own hooks); checked whether renderHud, refreshSheets or the visibility pass call it (hud.mjs:406-627, clock.mjs:940-954, visibility.mjs:1088: none); checked that the crossing writes no actor in an Eclipse (movement.mjs:2781-2802) and that keepMounted's observer redraws only when the node is gone (player-status.mjs:157-180). The file's own note says the stores fire no updateSetting (667), which is Foundry's own behaviour for client settings as the module reads it, not measured here. R1013 holds the setting list only, and R997 reads the rows pure with handed-in counts. A student's actor write elsewhere at the table repaints a GM's strip at once (relevant() is any student on a GM), so on a busy GM screen the gap is short; on the player's own strip it lasts until that player's own actor changes.
findings.probe: Headless: in an Eclipse with allowance 2, a player's client moves its token across one door; read #drpg-player-status .drpg-free-move on that client before and after the copy lands (both feet lit after = the gap), and on the GM the is-move field's text

findings.title: The four explainers opened from the clock, the Despair bar, the strip and the Projects tray are snapshots: the clock, the actions and the pools they print do not follow a change
findings.where: scripts/explain.mjs:49-58 (explainer), 232-251, 266-310, 314- (the bodies), 428-433 (the panels that open them)
findings.what_happens: explainer() opens a kit window with the body built once and no `live` option, and explain.mjs has no keepLive, keepFresh or hook. "Where things stand" prints the campaign, chapter and day, the phase with this character's own actions (R4106) and the time of day; the Despair one each pool's held / max and the overflow's hat; the strip's one the actions and Hope. A clock moved, a pool spent or an action taken while it stands leaves it on the old numbers, beside a clock, bar or strip that has already redrawn. A second click on the panel closes it and opens a fresh one (explainOnce, 476-482).
findings.failure_scenario: A player opens "Where things stand" to read how many actions they have this Morning, the GM moves the clock to Noon, and the window goes on saying Morning and the old count beside a clock that says Noon.
findings.expected: the body redrawn in place on the clock, the pools, the overflow and the character, as the panel beside it is (keepLive with the clock's and the despair kind's hooks and the actor)
findings.refutation_tried: Searched explain.mjs for live, keepLive, keepFresh and Hooks: none (grep); drpgWindow starts keepLive only when `live` is passed (ui-kit.mjs:1340). Looked for a recorded decision that the explainers are snapshots by design: none found in the file's comments; the owner's standing rule of 20.11.2026 covers every window that shows what changes.
findings.probe: game.drpg.explainState() on a player, then a GM's clock write (setClock to the next time of day); read .drpg-explain-body text on the player before and after

findings.title: The overflow caption's tooltip, which holds the GM's real count and why a full counter has not fired, can never show on a desk layout: the caption takes no pointer
findings.what_happens: #drpg-despair is pointer-events none so the canvas takes clicks through it, and its interactive parts opt back in by name: the row, the pip, the button, the name and the count. The caption (.drpg-overflow-caption) and the heading are not in that list, and no other rule in the seven stylesheets names the caption with pointer-events (script over every rule naming the panel: 2 rules, both listed here). So the caption inherits none and is never hit, and its `title` - the GM's "Spilled Despair: {count} of {max} ...", "This time of day is darkened. {count} of {max} spilled Despair is waiting ...", the player's "Only the GMs see the count" - is never shown. The caption draws at most the threshold (despair.mjs:1131), so the real count past it is in the tooltip only, as the function's note says (1119). A click on the caption also falls through to the canvas instead of opening the Despair explainer. On the narrow stack #drpg-column > * gives the panel pointer-events auto (narrow.css:80), and there it works.
findings.failure_scenario: A GM sees "Despair overflow · 20/20" with no darkening card and hovers the caption to read why and how much is really spilled: nothing appears, in either theme, on a desk screen.
findings.expected: the caption in the opt-in list (or its words where the GM can read them)
findings.refutation_tried: Listed every rule naming the Despair panel or the caption with pointer-events across styles/*.css (2: the panel's none and the opt-in list); stained-glass.css's rules for the panel (2731, 2287, 3863) set type and colour only. Foundry's own core stylesheet was not read: a universal rule there giving #ui-top's descendants the pointer would refute this, but then the module's own opt-in list (whose note says without it the pips do nothing) would not have been needed. Not hovered in a browser.
findings.probe: Chromium on audit/glass-harness.html or a table, a GM, 1366x768, both themes: document.elementFromPoint at the centre of #drpg-despair .drpg-overflow-caption (expect the canvas or a parent outside the panel, not the caption)

findings.title: The Sound window's Music tab does not follow the world's playlists, and its two switches and the Effects tab do not follow another GM
findings.control: a state's playlist selects; Music on; Vary the sounds; an effect's file path
findings.what_happens: The Music tab's selects list game.playlists as they stood when the window opened (musicMapTable from sortedPlaylists), and their live region is woken by the setting musicMap alone (449). A playlist created, renamed or deleted in the Playlists sidebar with the window open is not offered, keeps its old name, or stays selectable until the window is reopened; the no-playlists box above the table is outside any region. The Play tab's cue pane does follow the six playlist hooks (427-437), so the window is half live on the same documents - the F17 note at 120-135 describes this exact fault for the cue pane and its cure. The two world switches (musicEnabled, sfxVary) and the Effects tab's rows (sfxMap) have no region, so another GM's change is not drawn; a typed path saved from the stale field writes over it (sfx.mjs:776).
findings.failure_scenario: A GM with the Sound window open on Music creates a playlist "Trial theme" in the sidebar to map it: no select offers it until the window is closed and opened again, while the Play tab beside it already lists the cue playlist's new tracks.
findings.expected: the map's region woken by the playlist hooks too, and the switches and the Effects rows in live regions of their own
findings.refutation_tried: Read the window's two keepLive calls whole (sound-panel.mjs:418-452) and drpgWindow's own live option (not passed); the comment at 439-445 says only that another module setting does not wake the map, nothing of playlists. musicMap's write by another GM does redraw the rows (the 27.10 amend), so that half is live. The cue pane's hooks are on a different region and do not rebuild the map.
findings.probe: openSoundDialog() on a GM, the Music tab shown; Playlist.create({ name: "probe" }); read the options of select[name='state:dailyLife'] (no "probe" = the gap)

findings.title: Despair Flow's Overflow tab keeps the rules it opened with: another GM's change is not drawn, and Save writes the old rules back
findings.control: the rules form (threshold, each rule's toggle and size)
findings.where: scripts/gm-team-dialog.mjs:316-333 (keepFresh on the count line only), 159-160 (Save reads the form); scripts/overflow.mjs:110-138 (setOverflowRules), 1188-1258 (the pane)
findings.what_happens: The tab's one live part is the Right now line (keepFresh on the setting overflow and drpgOverflowChanged). The threshold and the thirteen rules are drawn from overflowRules once, and nothing listens to that setting here; the drawn darkening's row mark (is-drawn) and the suggestion line are drawn once too. Save reads the whole form (readOverflowForm) and setOverflowRules takes each field that carries a value, so a second GM's threshold or rule written meanwhile is replaced by what this form shows. The comment that chose this says none of it changes underneath the GM - true for one GM, not with two.
findings.failure_scenario: GM A has Despair Flow open; GM B lowers the threshold from 20 to 16 in their own copy and saves; A renames a pool and presses Save: the threshold is 20 again, and A's form never showed 16.
findings.expected: the rules form follows overflowRules (redrawn in place, rule 1 holding a field being typed in), or Save writes only what this GM changed
findings.refutation_tried: Read setOverflowRules (overflow.mjs:110-138): an edit without a value keeps the current, but readOverflowForm hands every toggle's checked state and every stepper's number, so every field carries one. Looked for another keepLive or hook in gm-team-dialog.mjs (keepFresh at 326 only; wireMonokumaLive and wireAssignmentLive are the other tabs'). With one GM nothing differs; the two-GM table is the module's supported case (the bridge's primary).
findings.probe: Two GMs (61-gmstore-case's gm2): open Despair Flow on gm1, setOverflowRules({ threshold: 16 }) on gm2, read [name=ovf-threshold] on gm1, press Save on gm1, read overflowRules().threshold

findings.title: The Voice section names the push-to-talk key it was built with: after its own Change the key, it still shows the old key
findings.surface: The Voice section of the settings window
findings.what_happens: The key line is written once from pushToTalkKey() when the fieldset is built, and the button beside it opens Foundry's Configure Controls; nothing listens for the binding's change, so after a player rebinds the key there and comes back, the line names the old one until the settings window is reopened. The device list is the same: the micNote drawn before the browser allowed the microphone stays after it does.
findings.failure_scenario: A player presses Change the key, binds push to talk to V in Foundry's window, closes it, and the settings window beside it still says "Push-to-talk key: `".
findings.expected: the line read again when Configure Controls closes or the binding changes
findings.refutation_tried: settings-window.mjs mounts the fieldset once (placeVoice, 360-365) and has no redraw for it (grep for keepLive and Hooks in it found none); the tile's own tooltip reads the key at each paint (voice-tile.mjs:978), so only this line lags.

not_established: Nothing was pressed or run (rule 2): every row is a source reading at b5a29e73. No base-run.json, probe-42.json or probe-43.json stood in audit/findings-1.2.118/ when this was read; the tests and scenarios named were found by grep and their results were not read.

Whether Foundry 14 fires `updateSetting` for a client-scope setting (the GMs' stores and their copies). player-status.mjs:667 says it does not, and finding 1 rests on that; new live check: at a table in an Eclipse, a player crosses one door and the status strip's feet are read on that player and the GM's Still placing on the GM.

Finding 3's last step: Foundry's own core stylesheet for #ui-top / #ui-middle descendants was not read. New live check: on a desk screen, hover the overflow caption as a GM in both themes and read whether its tooltip shows (or document.elementFromPoint at its centre).

The voice list's held reasons on a GM (moduleHoldsMic: a death the GMs keep, a mask, a veil): whether each change is followed by a permission write that repaints the list (updateUser) was traced for the veil (mask-gm.mjs: the block is C6's) but not for a death kept secret. A wrong button there is refused at the press with its reason, so at worst it is shown enabled until the next repaint.
The Effects tab's rows are sfx.mjs's (not a lane file): their wiring was read (sfx.mjs:727-790), their markup was not.

The windows the corner's launchers open (the GM panel, the messenger and its roster, the settings window, the handbooks) and the room tile and Event panel under the clock are other lanes' files and were not read here beyond the launcher's handler.
